_comment: Reverse-engineered schema of Claude Code's on-disk transcript format (~/.claude/projects/<project-slug>/<session-uuid>.jsonl + sibling <session-uuid>/ dir). Derived by inspecting real transcripts, not from any spec. Everything marked "verified" was empirically confirmed against real files listed in _evidence_sources; everything marked "inferred" or "unverified" was not.

_evidence_sources.main_transcript_studied: 7ed6ed2d-730b-4fbd-969a-802f848d8ccc.jsonl (2115 lines, CLI version 2.1.233, still growing at capture time -- it is the live session that produced this file)
_evidence_sources.oldest_transcript_compared: d6639916-4a41-45d6-b262-74efb81988db.jsonl (578 lines, CLI version 2.1.121, earliest by mtime among 82 transcripts)
_evidence_sources.caveat: Numbers for the newest transcript are a snapshot; the file is the live session doing this analysis (agent af33f01502a60e89f, desc 'Map transcript schema for costing', is this very task) and grows with every turn.

directory_layout.main_transcript: <project-dir>/<session-uuid>.jsonl -- one JSON object per line, the primary (non-sidechain) conversation.
directory_layout.sibling_dir: <project-dir>/<session-uuid>/ -- created alongside the main transcript file, same UUID as basename.
directory_layout.sibling_dir_subagents: <project-dir>/<session-uuid>/subagents/agent-<agentId>.jsonl + agent-<agentId>.meta.json -- one pair per spawned Agent-tool dispatch that actually produced turns. Present only in sessions that used the async Agent tool; seen as far back as the oldest CLI version sampled that used it (2.1.121), so this is a usage-gated feature, not something added between 2.1.121 and 2.1.233.
directory_layout.sibling_dir_tool_results: <project-dir>/<session-uuid>/tool-results/<id>.txt -- spillover storage for large tool outputs (big file reads, WebFetch bodies, etc.) that got persisted to disk instead of being inlined in the JSONL. Referenced from tool_result content blocks inside the (sub)agent JSONL by an id embedded in the content; not observed referenced from the main transcript directly in the session studied -- reads happened inside subagents there. Not part of token accounting itself (the tokens for that content are already counted in the message.usage of whichever call read/fetched it).
directory_layout.unrelated_subagents_workflows_dirs: Sibling top-level dirs named 'C--...-subagents-workflows-wf-<uuid>' (seen for the NANDI project, not Almacen) are NOT transcripts. They contain <session-uuid>/workflows/scripts/*.js -- JS orchestration scripts (meta/phase/agent/parallel DSL) that define a multi-agent workflow run (e.g. 'nandi-cerrar-gate-rojo'), generated by some workflow-orchestration tooling used in that project. Unrelated to token/cost accounting; do not treat as transcript data.

line_types._comment: Counts below are from the newest transcript (7ed6ed2d...), main file only, 2115 lines, captured 2026-08-19. Percentages will vary session to session.

attachment.description: UI/system bookkeeping events, keyed by attachment.type (hook_success, total_tokens_reminder, hook_non_blocking_error, hook_additional_context, queued_command, skill_listing, command_permissions, plan_mode, plan_mode_exit, deferred_tools_delta, opened_file_in_ide, auto_mode, plan_mode_reentry, edited_text_file, agent_listing_delta, mcp_instructions_delta, auto_mode_exit, date_change). Never carries message.usage -- not part of token accounting.
attachment.gotcha: attachment.type == 'total_tokens_reminder' contains text like '<total_tokens>15000000 tokens left</total_tokens>' -- this is a generic/static context-budget UI reminder, NOT a real per-session token total. Do not use it as a usage source.

assistant.description: One per model turn (including tool_use-only turns). message is an Anthropic Messages-API-shaped object: {role, model, content[], usage, id, ...}. This is the ONLY line type observed carrying message.usage in both main and subagent transcripts.
assistant.note_subagent_variant: In subagent transcripts, assistant lines additionally carry 'agentId' and 'attributionAgent' keys.

user.description: Real user turns AND synthetic tool_result turns (message.content[].type == 'tool_result'). toolUseResult carries a structured, tool-specific summary of the result -- for an async Agent-tool dispatch this is the primary join point (see agent_dispatch_join).
user.note_subagent_variant: In subagent transcripts, user lines also carry 'agentId' but drop 'toolUseResult'-adjacent orchestrator-only fields like 'origin'/'toolDenialKind'/'userFeedback' in the sample inspected.

ai-title.description: Auto-generated short session title, no usage/model data. First observed at CLI version 2.1.220; absent from every 2.1.121 transcript scanned -- version-gated addition.

mode.description: Records permission/interaction mode changes ('normal', etc.), separate from 'permission-mode'. First observed at 2.1.220; absent from every 2.1.121 transcript scanned -- version-gated addition.

last-prompt.description: Snapshot of the most recent user prompt text, for resume/UI purposes. Present at 2.1.121 already -- not new.

agent-name.description: Auto-generated short slug for the session (distinct from subagent agentId). Present at 2.1.121 already -- not new.

queue-operation.description: Async-agent lifecycle notifications. content is an XML-ish string containing <task-id>, <tool-use-id>, <output-file>, <status>, <summary> -- a third, redundant confirmation of the Agent-tool join key (task-id == subagent agentId == tool-use-id of the originating Agent tool_use). Present at 2.1.121 already -- not new.

file-history-delta.description: Plan-file / tracked-file backup bookkeeping. Not observed in the 2.1.121 sample; observed from 2.1.220 onward in the broader scan -- likely version-gated but not exhaustively confirmed absent at every pre-2.1.220 version.

system.description: Hook execution / local-command output records (subtype e.g. 'local_command'). No usage.

usage.carried_by: message.usage, on 'assistant' lines only (confirmed: 0 usage objects found on any other type across the whole transcript).

keys.input_tokens: Uncached prompt-token delta for this turn. Empirically near-constant (2, or 0 once) across all 460 assistant lines in the main transcript and all 643 in subagent transcripts sampled -- consistent with essentially the entire prompt (system prompt, tool defs, history) being served from cache_creation or cache_read, and input_tokens covering only what wasn't cacheable this call.
keys.output_tokens: Tokens generated this turn (includes thinking tokens; output_tokens_details.thinking_tokens is a sub-count, not additive on top).
keys.cache_creation_input_tokens: Total tokens written to cache this call. Verified equal to cache_creation.ephemeral_1h_input_tokens + cache_creation.ephemeral_5m_input_tokens in every sample checked (0 mismatches).
keys.cache_read_input_tokens: Tokens served from an existing cache entry (cache hit) this call.

cache_creation.ephemeral_5m_input_tokens: 5-minute-TTL cache write tokens (maps to pricing.json cache_write).
cache_creation.ephemeral_1h_input_tokens: 1-hour-TTL cache write tokens (maps to pricing.json cache_write_1h).

output_tokens_details.thinking_tokens: Subset of output_tokens spent on extended-thinking content; NOT additive -- do not add to output_tokens.

keys.speed: e.g. 'standard' -- unverified what other values exist.
keys.inference_geo: e.g. 'not_available' -- unverified what other values exist.
keys.iterations: Array, either absent (null, ~33% of lines) or exactly one element mirroring the top-level input_tokens/output_tokens/cache_* fields verbatim (0 mismatches, 0 cases with length != 1 across 1112 usage-bearing lines checked). Safe to ignore for totals -- summing iterations[] instead of the top-level fields would not double- or under-count in every case observed, but only because len(iterations) was always 0 or 1; do not assume this holds universally.

no_double_counting_conclusion.claim: Total context consumed for a call = input_tokens + cache_creation_input_tokens + cache_read_input_tokens (three non-overlapping buckets), and output_tokens is separate from all three.
no_double_counting_conclusion.evidence: input_tokens is trivially small (2 or 0) on literally every one of 1112 usage-bearing lines sampled across the main transcript and all 34 subagent transcripts, while cache_creation_input_tokens and cache_read_input_tokens carry the real prompt-size magnitude (tens of thousands to low millions per call). This is only consistent with input_tokens excluding the cached counts -- if it included them, a multi-hundred-turn session with a large, mostly-static system prompt could not show input_tokens pinned at ~2 the entire time. Matches documented Anthropic Messages API semantics (input_tokens = fresh/uncached tokens only).

model_attribution.field: message.model, on 'assistant' lines. No other top-level field carries a model id.

models_seen_all_subagent_transcripts_com.claude-sonnet-5: ~366-417 depending on capture instant (session was live/growing)

model_attribution.synthetic_model_note: message.model == '<synthetic>' appears on a handful of lines with all-zero usage -- these look like locally-synthesized turns (e.g. injected error/status turns), not real API calls. Exclude '<synthetic>' from cost calculations; verified their usage totals are 0 in every case observed but the mechanism that produces them was not traced further.

resolvedModel_field.location: message.toolUseResult.resolvedModel, on the 'user' line holding the tool_result for an Agent tool_use call (async dispatch).
resolvedModel_field.description: Gives the model the dispatch actually resolved to, sometimes with a context-window suffix, e.g. 'claude-opus-5[1m]' seen once (1M-context variant) vs plain 'claude-opus-5' elsewhere. When Agent tool input.model is a bare alias ('opus', 'sonnet'), resolvedModel is the corresponding full id (claude-opus-5, claude-sonnet-5) and matches message.model inside the subagent's own assistant lines exactly, 34/34 in the sample. When input.model is omitted (None), resolvedModel was observed as either claude-opus-5[1m] or claude-fable-5 depending on subagent_type/context -- inheritance rule not fully characterized, only empirically observed per-dispatch.

sidechain_semantics.evidence: Across the entire main transcript (2115 lines), isSidechain is False on every line that has it (1575 lines) and absent on the rest (540 lines, all of the session-scoped summary types like ai-title/mode/etc. that don't carry the field at all) -- never True. Across all 34 subagent transcript files (1150+ lines with the field), isSidechain is True on every single line. The main transcript and the subagents/ files are therefore a clean partition: subagent turns are NEVER inlined into the main .jsonl in this format version -- they live exclusively in <session-uuid>/subagents/agent-<agentId>.jsonl.

other_fields_tying_a_line_to_a_spawned_a.agentId: Present on every line inside a subagent's own .jsonl (assistant/user/attachment), equal to the <agentId> in that file's name.
other_fields_tying_a_line_to_a_spawned_a.parentUuid_chains: Present and forms a normal linear chain WITHIN a subagent transcript (first line's parentUuid is null, subsequent lines chain via uuid/parentUuid) -- but does NOT cross into the main transcript. It does not itself identify which Agent dispatch a subagent belongs to; use the join key instead.
other_fields_tying_a_line_to_a_spawned_a.slug: Present on most line types; appears to be a per-session or per-line UI slug, not observed to vary meaningfully per-agent in the sample -- not a reliable agent identifier.
other_fields_tying_a_line_to_a_spawned_a.attributionAgent / attributionSkill / at: Present on assistant lines; attributionAgent looks like it could record which named subagent-definition (e.g. 'Explore', 'general-purpose') produced the turn, but this was not cross-verified against agentType in meta.json in this pass -- treat as unverified/inferred, not confirmed.

agent_dispatch_join.summary: A given Agent tool_use in the main (or a parent) transcript CAN be reliably linked to its subagent's own turns and usage. There are three corroborating join points; the join was validated 34/34 (every Agent tool_use in the transcript matched exactly one subagents/agent-*.meta.json, and vice versa -- no orphans either direction).

join_keys.name: toolUseId <-> meta.json.toolUseId
join_keys.how: The main transcript's assistant line has a message.content[] entry with {type:'tool_use', name:'Agent', id:<tool_use_id>, input:{model, description, subagent_type, ...}}. The sibling file <session-uuid>/subagents/agent-<agentId>.meta.json contains {agentType, description, toolUseId, spawnDepth} where toolUseId equals that tool_use id exactly. The subagent's own transcript is <session-uuid>/subagents/agent-<agentId>.jsonl, and agentId equals the meta.json's filename fragment.

join_keys.name: toolUseResult.agentId (fastest, no extra file read needed)
join_keys.how: The 'user' line in the main transcript holding the tool_result for that same tool_use id has toolUseResult = {isAsync:true, status:'async_launched', agentId, description, resolvedModel, prompt}. agentId here is the same id used in the subagents/agent-<agentId>.jsonl filename -- this single field gives you the join, the dispatched model, and the original task description without opening the meta.json.

join_keys.name: queue-operation notification (weakest, UI-facing)
join_keys.how: type:'queue-operation' lines carry content as an XML-ish string with <task-id>agentId</task-id> and <tool-use-id>...</tool-use-id>, plus an <output-file> path under the OS temp dir. Redundant with the two keys above; useful only as a third confirmation, not needed for the join itself.

agent_dispatch_join.caveat: The join was validated only for direct children of the top-level session in one transcript. Nested/forked agents (spawnDepth > 1, seen as a meta.json field) were present in principle (the field exists) but this pass did not specifically hunt for and validate a 2-level-deep join; treat multi-level nesting as inferred-supported-but-not-directly-verified.

totals_example._comment: Concrete numbers computed from the newest transcript (7ed6ed2d-730b-4fbd-969a-802f848d8ccc), main file + all 34 files under its subagents/ dir, captured 2026-08-19T02:05:23 local. This session was LIVE and still growing at capture time (it is the session running this very investigation), so re-running the aggregation later will yield slightly larger sonnet/opus totals for the still-open subagent. Numbers are token counts, not cost.
totals_example.note: No haiku usage appears in this session at all -- the user's hypothesis that subagents ran on 'sonnet and haiku' was only half right for this session: subagents ran on a mix of sonnet, opus, and fable-5 depending on the model param passed to the Agent tool call (or its resolution when omitted); haiku simply wasn't dispatched this session.

stability_caveats.version_field: Present as top-level 'version' (e.g. '2.1.233') on conversation-chain line types (assistant/user/attachment/system) but ABSENT on session-summary line types (ai-title/mode/last-prompt/permission-mode/agent-name/queue-operation/file-history-delta/file-history-snapshot) -- so version can't be read off every line, only most of them.

key_set_drift_oldest_vs_newest.note: 'removed_in_newer' for imagePasteIds is presence-in-this-file-only, not confirmed as a removed feature -- it's plausibly still emitted conditionally (e.g. only on turns with pasted images) and simply didn't occur in the newest sample.

stability_caveats.general_conclusion: The format is actively evolving release to release (new top-level keys, new line types like ai-title/mode). A cost calculator should read message.usage defensively (all fields optional except input_tokens/output_tokens which were present on every usage-bearing line seen) and should NOT assume the top-level key set of assistant/user lines is fixed.
